why: learning_order_screen.dart:49-53 builds the AppBar title as a raw string concatenation ending in the literal 'Order' — never routed through AppLocalizations — even though every other user-facing string in the same file (resetToDefaultOrder tooltip, noItemsToOrder, controlledByParent) correctly uses AppLocalizations. The sibling per-track reorder screen already does this right: app_en.arb/app_he.arb define trackReorderScreenTitle ('{curriculum} • Reorder', translated), but no equivalent key exists for this whole-curriculum screen. Every Hebrew-locale user who opens this screen sees an app-bar title reading '<curriculum name> Order' with 'Order' rendered in English inside an otherwise-Hebrew UI. Neither widget test in this batch can catch it: learning_order_screen_test.dart asserts only Scaffold presence, and learning_order_screen_reset_test.dart asserts only the reordered list's contents — neither checks the app-bar text, and neither pumps a Locale('he') variant (TQ-3), so the defect has zero test surface.
recommendation: Add an ARB key (EN+HE) for this screen's title mirroring trackReorderScreenTitle's shape, e.g. learningOrderScreenTitle: '{curriculum} Order' (EN) with a proper Hebrew ICU translation, and use AppLocalizations.of(context)!.learningOrderScreenTitle(curriculumLabelText(...)) instead of the raw string concatenation. Extend one of this batch's widget tests to pump under Locale('he') and assert the app-bar text does not contain the literal ASCII substring 'Order' (or assert the exact localized string).
acceptance_criteria: learning_order_screen.dart's AppBar title comes entirely from AppLocalizations — no raw string literal concatenated onto the curriculum label.
New ARB key present in both app_en.arb and app_he.arb; make arb-parity still reports full EN/HE parity.
A widget test pumps LearningOrderScreen under Locale('he') and asserts the rendered title is the localized string (or explicitly asserts it does not contain 'Order').
